first_impression.reaction: Googled 'short wedding vows' because I don't want to stand up there reading an essay. The intro opens with a claim I can't check, but the next paragraph tells me exactly what's on the page, including the legal words. Went straight to the FAQ, then the legal section. The legal section is the best part: dated, linked to the actual Act, quoted word for word. Examples are fine and short as promised. The planner pitch turns up in the middle of the legal section, which is the wrong place for it, and nothing anywhere says what the planner costs.

journey.quote: Short wedding vows suit that instinct, and they land harder than most long ones.
journey.reaction: Says who? Opinion dressed up as fact. Minor, but it's the first thing I read.

journey.quote: Below are 20 original examples, each written to be spoken in well under a minute, grouped by tone and occasion.
journey.reaction: Clear contents list. I know what I'm getting and I can check the 'under a minute' claim myself. I did, roughly. It holds.

journey.quote: In Australia, when your celebrant is not a minister of religion, it is sufficient for each of you to say the section 45(2) words, or words to that effect, in the presence of the celebrant and witnesses.
journey.reaction: Straight answer with the section number. That's the minimum I legally have to say. Good.

journey.section: What words do you legally have to say when you marry in Australia?
journey.quote: As at November 2026, the form of the ceremony sits in section 45 of the Marriage Act 1961, and the celebrant's explanation sits in section 46.
journey.reaction: A date, an Act and section numbers, with links to the legislation. Exactly what I'd check, and I can check it in one click.

journey.section: What words do you legally have to say when you marry in Australia?
journey.quote: Ask your celebrant how your own vows fit around the legal ones, and raise it when you sit down together to lodge your notice of intended marriage.
journey.reaction: Admits the page isn't the final word and points me to the person who is. Fair.

journey.quote: In New Zealand, couples can write their own vows as long as each says words to the effect of "I [name] take you [name] to be my legal wife/husband/partner".
journey.reaction: The Australian bit links to the Act. This one has no source link at all. Where does it come from?

journey.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, one Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact.
journey.reaction: Sales pitch wedged into the legal section, before I've even seen a vow. And 'payments' again. Do you take a cut from the venue?

journey.section: What are some good short wedding vows?
journey.quote: Each of these is our own writing, and yours to adapt.
journey.reaction: Good, not lifted from somewhere else. Saves me checking whether I'm reading someone's copied list.

journey.section: What are good short vows for him and for her?
journey.quote: Each runs well under a minute and can be adapted for any couple by changing the final word.
journey.reaction: Only half true. 13 and 15 end on 'husband' and 'wife', but 14 and 16 don't have a gendered word to change. Small, but I notice things like that.

journey.section: How do you say your vows with confidence?
journey.quote: Ask your venue whether a microphone is available for the ceremony, who sets it up, and whether you can test it at the rehearsal.
journey.reaction: Practical. That's the kind of thing that goes wrong on the day and nobody owns it. I'd put this in the spreadsheet.

journey.quote: If that is your plan, Wedded Concierge can carry the logistics while you work on the words.
journey.reaction: Second pitch. Still no price, no fee model.

journey.section: Saying it in your own words
journey.quote: Where you say them, and who flies in to hear them, is where a Wedded Advisor comes in.
journey.reaction: Nice line, tells me nothing. What does the Advisor cost and who pays them? Same silence as every other planner site.

unanswered_questions: Where does the New Zealand vow wording come from? Link the official source like you did for the Marriage Act.
Can our own vows replace the section 45(2) words entirely if they're 'words to that effect', or do we have to say the legal wording as well? Who decides, the celebrant?
Does Wedded Concierge handle 'payments' by passing supplier prices through at cost, or is there a commission or mark-up? (deferred business detail)
How is the Wedded Wonderland fee calculated, and what's a realistic 'from AUD' figure? (deferred business detail)
Show me a real destination wedding you've planned with the actual budget. (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: Short wedding vows suit that instinct, and they land harder than most long ones.
turn_offs_found.why: Unsupported claim in the opening paragraph; opinion stated as fact.

turn_offs_found.quote: Through Wedded Concierge, one Wedded Advisor plans the venue, travel, vendors and payments with you, anywhere in the world, as your single point of contact.
turn_offs_found.why: CTA before the evidence: it sits in the legal section, before any vow examples, and 'payments' raises the commission question without answering it.

turn_offs_found.quote: Where you say them, and who flies in to hear them, is where a Wedded Advisor comes in.
turn_offs_found.why: Emotional framing in place of a fee model or commission disclosure at the point where I'm asked to enquire.

would_share_with: My fiancee: the five-part template and example 8 ('Three promises.')
Our Reddit thread: the legal section with the section 45(2) and 46(1) wording and links to the Act

cta_reaction.quote: Start a conversation through Wedded Concierge, and for more ceremony ideas, read the Wedded Wonderland magazine.
cta_reaction.why: Useful, well-sourced vows article and I'd use the legal section. But it's a vows article, and three pitches in, nothing tells me what the planner costs or whether you take a cut from suppliers. I'd keep comparing.

top_3_changes: Move the Wedded Concierge line out of the 'Marrying overseas' legal section and below the vow examples, so the pitch follows the useful content instead of interrupting it.
Link an official source for the New Zealand vow wording, the same way the Marriage Act is linked, and fix the FAQ line about 'changing the final word', which doesn't apply to examples 14 and 16.
Near the closing CTA, state how the Wedded Wonderland fee works and whether supplier commissions apply (deferred business detail); drop or soften 'they land harder than most long ones'.
